questions.q: What is the typical physical state of ionic compounds at room temperature (25°C)?
Why do ionic compounds have very high melting and boiling points?
a: They are made of soft molecules
A vast amount of thermal energy is required to overcome the strong electrostatic forces holding the giant ionic lattice together
They evaporate easily at room temperature

questions.q: Do solid ionic compounds (like dry sodium chloride crystals) conduct electricity?
a: Yes, but only in the dark
No, because the ions are fixed in position within the crystal lattice and cannot move
No, because they contain no electrical charges

questions.q: Under what conditions can ionic compounds conduct electricity?
a: Only when exposed to strong magnets
When molten (liquid) or dissolved in water, because the ions are free to move

questions.q: What happens when an ionic crystal is struck firmly with a hammer?
a: It shatters or cleaves cleanly because like-charged ions are pushed next to each other, causing repulsion
It stretches into a long wire
It melts instantly into a gas

questions.q: Are ionic compounds generally soluble in water, and why?
a: No, they never dissolve in any solvent
Yes, because polar water molecules are attracted to and stabilize the charged ions, pulling them away from the lattice
Yes, because water reacts chemically to destroy them

questions.q: What is formed at the positive electrode (anode) when molten lead(II) bromide is electrolyzed?
Which term describes a liquid or solution that conducts electricity through the movement of ions?
Why do ionic solutions conduct electricity while pure distilled water does not?
a: Dissolved ions act as mobile charge carriers, whereas pure water has very few free ions
Water molecules stop moving in solutions
Distilled water contains too much oxygen

questions.q: What type of crystal lattice structure do ionic compounds form?
a: A giant ionic lattice of alternating positive and negative ions

questions.q: Which of the following substances has the highest melting point due to strong ionic bonding?
What happens to the electrical conductivity of solid sodium chloride when it is heated until it melts into a liquid?
a: It becomes a good electrical conductor because ions are free to move

questions.q: Why are ionic compounds generally insoluble in non-polar organic solvents like hexane?
a: Non-polar solvents cannot form attractive interactions with charged ions strong enough to break the ionic lattice
Hexane reacts to form an acid

questions.q: During the electrolysis of molten sodium chloride, what product is formed at the negative electrode (cathode)?
Which of the following best describes the appearance of most solid ionic compounds?
What term describes the brittleness of ionic solids when subjected to mechanical stress?
Why do ionic compounds not conduct electricity in the solid state?
a: The ions are locked tightly into fixed positions in the lattice and cannot move to carry charge
Solid ionic compounds contain no charges

questions.q: Which of the following ionic compounds would you expect to have a higher melting point: sodium chloride (NaCl) or magnesium oxide (MgO)?
a: Sodium chloride because it has smaller ions
Magnesium oxide because Mg^2+ and O^2- ions have higher charges, resulting in much stronger electrostatic attraction
Magnesium oxide has a lower melting point because it is a gas

questions.q: When sodium chloride dissolves in water, what happens to the sodium and chloride ions?
a: They react to form chlorine gas
They separate from each other and become hydrated by water molecules
They precipitate out as solid rock

questions.q: What is the role of ions in an electrolyte during electrolysis?
a: They migrate toward the oppositely charged electrodes, carrying electrical current

questions.q: Which physical property is *not* characteristic of typical ionic compounds?
a: High volatility (turning to gas easily at room temperature)
Electrical conductivity when molten or dissolved

questions.q: What causes the high hardness observed in many ionic crystalline solids?
a: Strong electrostatic attractions throughout the giant lattice making planes difficult to shift

questions.q: How does the strength of ionic bonding affect the enthalpy change of melting for ionic salts?
a: It requires a high enthalpy of fusion to break the strong ionic bonds

questions.q: When copper(II) sulfate crystals are dissolved in water, what color is the resulting solution and why?
a: Bright red due to copper atoms
Blue due to the presence of hydrated copper(II) ions moving freely in solution

questions.q: Why do ionic substances tend to be odorless solids at room temperature?
a: They have extremely low vapor pressures because their ions are strongly bound in a giant lattice, preventing them from evaporating into gases
They are made of heavy metals

questions.q: In an experiment testing electrical conductivity, why does solid copper(``II'') chloride fail to light a bulb, while aqueous copper(``II'') chloride lights it brightly?
a: Ions are fixed in the solid crystal but are mobile and free to carry charge in aqueous solution

questions.q: What happens to a crystal of sodium chloride when placed in liquid water?
a: It sinks and remains unchanged forever
It dissolves as water molecules pull the sodium and chloride ions into solution

questions.q: Which of the following factors determines the magnitude of the lattice energy in an ionic compound?
a: The charges of the ions and the distance (radius) between them

questions.q: Why is it incorrect to speak of a single 'molecule' of sodium chloride (NaCl)?
a: Because NaCl exists as a continuous giant 3D lattice of alternating Na+ and ions rather than distinct, separate molecular units
Because sodium chloride is a gas
Because the formula is actually Na10Cl10

questions.q: What is the visual evidence that an ionic compound has dissolved in water to form a clear solution?
a: The liquid becomes cloudy with precipitate
The solid disappears completely and the liquid remains transparent (though possibly colored)
The volume of water decreases to zero

questions.q: How do ionic compounds respond when an electric field is applied across a molten salt?
a: Negative ions move toward the positive electrode while positive ions move toward the negative electrode
All ions move in random circles

questions.q: Which of the following statements explains why ionic compounds are brittle rather than malleable?
a: They are made of soft gases
They contain free electrons that repel each other
They can bend easily under pressure
Displacement of planes brings ions of the same charge next to each other, causing repulsive forces that fracture the crystal

questions.q: Why do molten ionic substances conduct electricity while molten covalent substances (like molten sulfur or sugar) generally do not?
a: Ionic substances produce mobile charged ions upon melting, whereas covalent substances consist of neutral molecules without free charges
Ionic substances contain free electrons like metals

questions.q: Which of the following is a correct safety precaution when handling molten ionic salts in a laboratory setting?
a: Touch them with bare hands to check temperature
Wear eye protection and safety screens because high-temperature ionic liquids can sputter or spit
Add cold water to boiling molten salt immediately

questions.q: What happens to the boiling point of ionic compounds as the electrostatic attraction between their constituent ions increases?
a: Boiling point decreases to room temperature

questions.q: Which of the following correctly pairs an ionic compound property with its microscopic cause?
a: Low melting point due to weak covalent bonds
Electrical conductivity in solids due to free electrons
Solubility in organic solvents due to non-polar charges
High melting point due to strong electrostatic forces throughout a giant lattice
